newsitem.title: USA: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - how hungry are dealers now?.
newsitem.headline: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - how hungry are dealers now?.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds on Wednesday recovered to flat from early losses of up to 3/4 of a point after the U.S. Treasury market rebounded, but traders questioned how much room dealers have left for new issues.

With a "mammoth" $4.8 billion of new municipal bonds expected to be sold this week, dealers still appear to be holding a number of these issues themselves. This could cut their buying interest for next week's new offerings, which includes some very large issues.

"There was a lot of two-way flow. Probably the Street is longer than it has been in awhile," a trader said. There was fairly heavy selling interest across the board revealed in the high number of bid wanted lists, traders said.

Whether enough customers will be found to mop up supply without depressing prices remains to be seen. "That's still questionable. You might get people interested but there is still so much out there," another trader said.

While Merrill Lynch, which won $713 million of New Jersey Transportation Trust Fund Authority bonds at a true interest cost of 5.4826 percent, had zero balance left, traders noted several other issues were repriced with higher yields.

For example, Bear Stearns & Co said it repriced $169 million of Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs mortgage revenues, raising yields on a number of maturities, including the top yield to 6.25 percent from 6.20 in 2028.

Still, traders said that forecasts that the market's early dip would produce bigger bargains were not borne out. "I thought buyers would want more of a yield, but it seems like the deals were done more in line with what was expected," a trader said.

Bonds in the secondary market that were actively quoted included Metropolitan Pier and Exposition Authority Illinois Dedicated State Tax Revenue Refundings of June 2027, which have a 5-1/4 percent coupon, and were offered at 5.84 percent net. This was two basis points higher than on Tuesday.
And Massachusetts State Water Resource Authority issues of November 2026, which have a 5.6 percent coupon, were bid at 5.86 percent net, unchanged.
